Users who rely on encrypted HFS+ drives will no longer need to decrypt them first before converting them to APFS for compatibility with macOS 28. Here's what that means.

Apple updates macOS 28 migration guidance for encrypted HFS+ drives

A few weeks ago, Apple published a support document explaining that starting with macOS 28, "the Mac OS Extended file system format will only be supported on unencrypted volumes (disks and other storage devices)."

This essentially means that users currently relying on encrypted HFS+ external drives or other encrypted volumes in legacy Mac formats will need to "decrypt or reformat any encrypted Mac OS Extended volumes," as Apple explains.

Previously, the support page offered step-by-step instructions for either decrypting the volume, or erasing and reformatting it to APFS.

Apple has now revised that page to add a third option, letting users convert encrypted HFS+ volumes directly to encrypted APFS without having to decrypt first. Apple now offers the following instructions for the new procedure:

Convert the volume to encrypted APFS Open Disk Utility, located in the Utilities folder of your Applications folder. Or use Spotlight to search for and open it. From the Show menu in the menu bar, choose Show Only Volumes. In the sidebar of Disk Utility, select the volume's name. From the Edit menu in the menu bar, choose Convert to APFS, then click Convert to confirm. Quit Disk Utility when finished.

However, Apple notes that "this method does not apply to encrypted Time Machine backup disks."

Apple has also removed the previous instructions for decrypting the volume first, converting it to APFS without erasing, and then optionally re-encrypting it.

To see the updated support page, click this link.

Will this new option make it easier for you to prepare your drives for upgrading to macOS 28? Let us know in the comments.
